newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan eases insurers' overseas investment rules.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan eases insurers' overseas investment rules.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Monday it would soon ease regulations governing overseas investments by the island's insurance companies in a drive to liberalise the market.

The ministry would let insurers invest 10 percent of its available funds in overseas investments, up from the current five percent, Cheng Chi-shih, head of the ministry's department of insurance, told reporters.
The new rules would take effect by the end of May, Cheng said.
Insurance companies would be allowed to buy securities and bonds in most stock exchanges, except for those issued by communist China and China-funded companies, Cheng said.
Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil split them in 1949.
Under present rules, insurers can only invest securities and bonds in 20 major exchanges.
After the liberalisation, the insurance firms can make foreign currency deposits in the world's top 500 banks instead of the top 100 banks, Cheng said.
The firms would also be permitted to set up overseas branches and merge with foreign insurance companies, Cheng said. He gave no further details.
